title: I'm addicted to vibing tiny games
author: lorean_victor
selftext:
Case in point, the tiny game in the video (you can play it [here](https://vibed.city/e/01a02421-4028-70cd-b7e7-82f115947699) if you want). I had other stuff planned for the day, woke up and had this idea, and had to try it to see how it would look like. I even got ChatGPT to pull some research on flock behaviour of sheep and model their behaviour scientifically 😅

Anyways this "addiction" started a few weeks back. We had a discussion with a friend about the idea of a place to share tiny interactive stuff. He of course [vibe coded that really quickly](https://vibed.city), he made plugins and MCPs, we added SDKs for shared storage and identity, and lots of guides to make the model make smooth and good looking interactions without much effort, so we can focus on the ideas mostly (which tbf still require quite a lot of back and forth to get smooth enough). We also added "remix" ability (mostly guide for the models to code the vibes in a remixable way), so that its super easy (and cheap token wise 😅) to iterate on other people's ideas.

The end result is that now I'm addicted to this loop of constantly playing stuff, remixing stuff, and vibing new stuff. Initially I thought of it as a place for testing interaction and game ideas quickly, but overtime it has become something of a "TikTok" or "McDonalds" of the joy of creating stuff for me. If creating a more complete game or experience is like a full meal, this way of quickly vibe coding tiny games is like getting a quick and easy snack. Which considering the fact that my job hasn't been game design and I don't have much time for it means I get to experience this thrill again, but I am also kind of addicted to these "quick snacks" instead of going for the proper meal.

Anyone else feeling the same? How are your experiences?
